title: Batch orchestrator ledger
description: Batch history for one programme's build run. Lives at <workarea>/orchestrator-ledger.json. Written only by L0. Records what each batch actually built; backlog.json remains the plan of record for increment truth. A batch is a budget, not a plan — L0 hands L1 a count and L1 re-derives the next increment after every landing, so the ids are known only as they land. Under the full lifecycle an increment is landed only once its PR is merged, the base branch is green and its ticket has reached jiraDoneStatus.

programme.description: The parameters a fresh L0 needs to resume without asking anyone.

workarea.description: Path under workareas/ holding backlog.json, e.g. shared/plant-products-ched-pp

branch.description: The BASE branch. Every increment cuts its own ticket-named branch off this one and merges back into it. Normally main

lifecycle.description: full = ticket, branch, PR, CI, merge, ticket Done per increment. local = commit on the current branch only, no Jira and no PR. Default full

jiraProject.description: Jira project key raised tickets land in, e.g. EUDPA. Absent when lifecycle is local

epic.description: The parent epic every raised ticket hangs off. Required when lifecycle is full

jiraInProgressStatus.description: The board's working status, set when an increment's build starts, e.g. In Progress. Board configuration, not a constant — confirm it with tools/jira/transition-ticket.sh <KEY> --list, never from a script's --help text. Recorded here so a later session can see which board wording this programme was built against

jiraDoneStatus.description: The board's finished status, set after the merge, e.g. Done. Same caveat as jiraInProgressStatus: confirm it against the board. A ticket at any other status, however final it reads, is not a landing

batchSize.description: The default per-batch budget — the MOST increments an L1 may build before returning. Not a target. Default 5

batches.description: Append-only, oldest first. Batch numbers are contiguous from 1.

budget.description: The count L0 handed L1 — the most increments it was allowed to build. Known before the batch starts, unlike the ids

startCounts.description: Backlog counts as L0 measured them when opening the batch. Lets a later reader compute a batch's progress without re-querying, and survives a dead L1

attempted.description: The ids L1 actually started, in the order it derived them. Absent while in flight. Kept alongside landed/notLanded because those two do not cover an increment L1 died partway through — reconciling an abandoned batch needs the list of ids to check against git. An id may legitimately appear here in more than one batch: a failed increment is retried by a later batch

status.description: in-flight = L1 spawned, not yet reported. landed = every increment L1 attempted landed. partial = some landed, then it stopped. failed = none landed. halted-at-gate = the loop stopped at a designed gate. abandoned = L1 died and L0 reconciled from git plus backlog.json. A batch that lands fewer increments than its budget is NOT partial — partial is about failure, not about spending the budget

endedEarly.description: Why L1 stopped. budget-spent means it used its full allowance; every other value means it returned early on purpose, which is a normal and desirable outcome

driver.description: How L1 drove L2 — the increment-build-loop Workflow, or the documented Codex fallback

scriptPath.description: The script the Workflow ran, normally the batch's fresh run copy at workareas/<workarea>/build-loop.run.js. Recorded alongside driver so a batch can be traced to the script that produced it. Absent when driver is codex-direct

commit.description: Short SHA on the base branch, verified by L0 against git log — not copied from L1's report unchecked. Under the full lifecycle this is the merge commit

repo.description: The increment's repo field: frontend, backend, tests, or both

ticket.description: The Jira key the increment was built under, e.g. EUDPA-12345. Its status is jiraDoneStatus by the time an increment reaches landed. Absent when lifecycle is local

prs.description: The merged pull request URLs, one per repo the increment touched — two for a cross-repo increment, backend first. Absent when lifecycle is local

outcome.description: ci-red = the PR never went green within its fix budget; it is still open and the ticket is still at jiraInProgressStatus. main-red = the base branch went red after a merge, or a second PR went red after the first merged; the run halted for a human. done-failed = merged and green, but the ticket would not transition to jiraDoneStatus — usually because that status is not what this board calls it, which detail names alongside the transitions the board does offer

ticket.description: The Jira key, where one was raised before the increment failed. Its status says where the lifecycle stopped

prs.description: Pull request URLs left OPEN by a failure. A red PR is never merged and never closed — a human reads it

branch.description: The increment's branch, PUSHED with the failed attempt committed as wip. This is how a failed attempt reaches another machine — prefer it to stash, which is machine-local. Full lifecycle only

wip.description: Short SHA of the wip commit holding the failed attempt on that branch

stash.description: The stash ref the rollback produced, so the work is recoverable on THIS machine. Local lifecycle only — a stash ref does not travel

report.description: Workarea-relative path to L1's full batch report, e.g. logs/batches/batch-003.md. L0 records the path and does not read the file
